title: Why Can't You See Most of Hawaii? (Look Down)

segments.text: Hawaiʻi's Big Island, with the ocean {m:drained}drained.
segments.visual: S4 GROUND hero. FRAME 1 = THUMBNAIL ARM A (NO OCEAN, round-3 default, packaging/final_ep02_1.jpg) IN MOTION. TerrainStage with the plate d3 settings (landSat 1.6, landGain 2.7, darker cool basalt and sediment; masked grade: saturated rainforest green and rust on the cap, cool slate flank, deeper blue sky top), VE 1.0. Camera lon -155.32, lat 18.42, 26 km up, looking north; framing = the 1.32 zoom crop (centre 0.47/0.49); frame 0 must score SSIM >= 0.8 at 320x180 (label off) against final_ep02_1.jpg. No water anywhere in frame. The thin, solid, terrain-following white line on today's 0 m coast is on from frame 0 (never dashed, straight or labelled). Motion from frame 0 that clears the still_s gate: push 4% per 10 s plus 0.6 deg/s heading drift. The thumbnail's 'NO OCEAN' text block is on frame 0 (same plate and place as the thumbnail); its 8 px accent bar wipes on over frames 2-10 (the first motion graphic before frame 10); the block dissolves out over 8 frames starting 0.6 s after {m:drained}. No gauge yet.
segments.music: Cold-open cue: airy, curious pulse from frame 1. No logo, no sting.

segments.text: {m:most}Most of this mountain is normally {m:under}underwater.
segments.visual: Same camera, push continues. At {m:most}: a 2.5 s eased tilt DOWN (pitch about -5 deg) along the south flank, from the white line toward the base (first hint of '(Look Down)'). At {m:under}: the white coast line brightens over 6 frames and back, so the eye finds where the sea normally stops. No text.

segments.text: The Hawaiʻi you see on {m:card}postcards? Only the {m:top}top.
segments.visual: Same drained camera; still NO water (the thumbnail state stays on screen until about 0:10). At {m:card}: a paper postcard (off-white #F6F1E4, a real public-domain photo of a Big Island coast, place name 'HAWAIʻI' in large postcard type, 2-4 px warm paper edge, soft contact shadow, same sun) drops from the top of frame and lands flat ONTO the dry summit cap above the white coast line, tilted 4 deg, roughly the cap's footprint in perspective, while the whole drained flank below stays bare. At {m:top}: the card lifts 10% on its paper hinge and the cap under it takes a hero-orange outline (#FF5A36, 55% fill, 5-6 px white outline) for 1.0 s: 'only the top', shown literally at true scale against everything below it.
sfx: paper_flap (-14) as the card lands on {m:card}

segments.text: Start with {m:maui}Maui, {m:molo}Molokaʻi and {m:lanai}Lānaʻi.
segments.visual: As s003 ends the postcard flutters off frame-right and an eased 2.0 s flight northwest begins (ease on the destination key). The sea refills to 0 m DURING the flight (live, foam rim, turquoise depth gradient); the flight lands on the arm B 'ONE ISLAND' composition (packaging/final_ep02_2.jpg camera: south of Lānaʻi, about 60 km up, looking NNW), VE 1.0, water at 0 m. Persistent SEA LEVEL gauge top-left (plate 12-15% of frame height, moving water marker, no running digits; hero mode shows one big number only at a hero-number moment) slides in during the flight. NAMES (packaging arm-B condition, by 0:14): ONE text block in the free upper third (Barlow 800 caps, 64 px cap or more, plate with accent bar), its three words revealed whole on their spoken words: MAUI at {m:maui}, MOLOKAʻI at {m:molo}, LĀNAʻI at {m:lanai}; at the same moments each island's coast gets a 6 px white rim pulse (0.6 s), so name and place match on the word. The block holds until the 'ONE ISLAND' beat in s006 (about 5 s; never three separate map labels at once). Kahoʻolawe is dimmed and desaturated from the moment the flight lands, no label.

segments.text: Drop the sea {m:fourhundred}four hundred {m:ft400}feet.
segments.visual: HERO SHOT #1 (arm B composition). S4 GROUND live drain: water eases 0 to -122 m over 3.5 s. At {m:fourhundred}: the gauge goes to hero mode: a yellow #FFD23F Anton counter (cap 150-190 px) rolls to '−400 FT' and lands exactly on {m:ft400}. The islands fuse during the drain (the ʻAuʻau saddle surfaces first, at about -50 m, then the Kalohi side at about -78 m); banks surface as cream-tan reef flats; Penguin Bank rises as a big flat lobe off West Molokaʻi. The names block stays up. Hold the live drain 3 s longer than the draft (retention review backfill).

segments.text: They become one {m:one}island.
segments.visual: Same camera; water held at -122 m (never below -150 m in this shot, or Kahoʻolawe joins). At {m:one}: the names block dissolves (6 frames) into the headline 'ONE ISLAND' in the same place; the fused island (Molokaʻi + Lānaʻi + West Maui + Haleakalā + Penguin Bank; outline from sill.py flood-fill at -122 m on the production grid) takes the hero-orange 55% fill and white outline. The Pailolo Channel stays water (a bay inside the horseshoe). Kahoʻolawe stays separate, dimmed and desaturated, no label; Oʻahu and the Big Island stay separate.

segments.text: That's not a what-if. In the last {m:ice}Ice Age, it really happened.
segments.visual: Low golden-hour pass (2.5 s, eased) over the dry land bridge between Lānaʻi and West Maui (the ʻAuʻau Channel floor near 20.885N 156.758W), camera 1.5 km up, VE 1.0, three seabirds crossing the dry channel at true scale. At {m:ice}: kicker 'LAST ICE AGE' in the top third for 2 s.

segments.text: No ferry {m:ferry}needed.
segments.visual: GAG (3.5 s), S11 paper standee on the real terrain. The recurring paper tourist (cut-out of a real public-domain 1950s Hawaiʻi tourist photo, aloha shirt; 2-4 px warm off-white paper edge, fold-out base tab, soft contact shadow, same sun) hop-walks across the dry ʻAuʻau Channel floor from Lānaʻi toward West Maui pulling a paper suitcase, at 35-40% of frame height, ground camera about 40 m up. The walk starts under the end of the previous line. At {m:ferry}: he tips his hat to camera. Never on the Pailolo side. Tourist appearance 1 of 4.
segments.humor: Deadpan: at the Ice Age low stand you could walk from Lānaʻi to Maui. 1.2 s music dip (-10 dB) right before the line; suitcase-wheel rattle in the gap after it.

segments.text: Keep draining. And {m:look}look down.
segments.visual: '(LOOK DOWN)' MOVE #1 (promise map: by about 0:27). At {m:look}: from the tourist the camera rises 300 m and pitches down 40 deg over Maui Nui's new north shore, then rides down the submarine slope as the water resumes falling (-122 m toward -1,000 m over 6 s; gauge marker dropping, no digits).

segments.text: Even with every drop gone, we won't hit {m:nobottom}bottom.
segments.visual: The camera keeps riding down the slope while the water falls away below it. At {m:nobottom}: the slope ahead fades into blue depth with no floor in sight (a tease; no text, no number). LOOP PLANTED (the film's one forward promise, the story's own question): paid by the Ch6 card 'WE HAVEN'T HIT BOTTOM', s160 and the payoff.

segments.text: The shore becomes a {m:ledge}ledge. Then the slope {m:plunge}plunges.
segments.visual: At {m:ledge}: the camera passes the edge of the shallow shelf; at {m:plunge}: it tips over and follows the submarine slope down (say 'plunges', never 'cliffs').

segments.text: See that flat {m:bank}bank? It was dry land once.
segments.visual: Eased 2 s pull-back and swing west: Penguin Bank, the big flat table off West Molokaʻi (top at about -30 to -60 m), stands high and dry above the falling water. At {m:bank}: hero-orange outline on the bank top; map label 'PENGUIN BANK'.

segments.text: The sea rose after the Ice Age and {m:drowned}drowned it.
segments.visual: At {m:drowned}: reverse drain, 3 s: the water rises from -1,000 m back to 0 m over Maui Nui; the land bridge and Penguin Bank go under and Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi separate again. Gauge marker climbs. (Backup title 2 condition: this line names cause 1, the sea rose; s014 names cause 2, sinking.)

segments.text: And the Big Island is sinking right {m:now}now.
segments.visual: Whip-pan (8 frames, motion blur) southeast to the Big Island's south coast, sea at 0 m, morning light. At {m:now}: one yellow down-arrow (15 px body) beside the coast pulses once (no number).

segments.text: Usually, that's slow. {m:notalways}Not always.
segments.visual: Eased push toward Kīlauea's south-flank coast while the light falls to pre-dawn blue. Music thins out on {m:notalways}.
segments.music: Cold-open cue resolves and thins to a low sustained pad (no sting).

segments.text: One night, campers were asleep at {m:hal}Halapē, a beach on this coast.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK, human story. Staged at a 1-3 km oblique (NOT at ground level: the look book rates close terrain 'not yet good enough') on the USGS 3DEP 10 m DEM blended with the NCEI coastal DEM at Halapē (pin from GNIS/NPS), pre-dawn blue light, stars: the cove, the coconut grove as instanced palms in the scene's own grade (not paper), a few small tents (no people shown), still water. At the start of the line: kicker 'NOVEMBER 1975' (small, free third, 2 s; the year is shown, not spoken, to keep the 60 s number cap). At {m:hal}: map label 'HALAPĒ' on its pin (holds 2 s). GATE: this staging must pass a 10-15 s phone motion test before lock of the render.

segments.text: Before dawn, a smaller earthquake woke them {m:woke}up.
segments.visual: At {m:woke}: a short tremor: the palms shiver, the water surface ripples, a lantern glow comes on inside one tent.

segments.text: More than an hour later, the big one {m:hit}hit.
segments.visual: Hold on the quiet cove for 1.5 s, then at {m:hit}: a hard jolt (camera shake 6 frames), dust off the low cliff behind the grove.

segments.text: The south coast {m:lurch}lurched toward the sea.
segments.visual: At {m:lurch}: the whole coastal block slides seaward in one move; quick pull-up to show a long stretch of coast moving together.

segments.text: The ground gave way. Parts of the shore {m:drop}dropped farther than a basketball hoop is high.
segments.visual: At {m:drop}: the coastal block subsides about 3.5 m in 1.5 s and the sea floods in among the palms. The palms STAY STANDING, now in about 1.2 m of water (visual truth). Scale: a side-on section inset in the free upper third (same grade as the scene, about 35% of frame height) shows the old ground line, the new one and a plain basketball pole-and-hoop silhouette at true scale (rim at 10 ft), drawn in the scene's own grade: no paper edge, no hinge, no wobble, no SFX (a scale marker, never a prop gag; deaths follow). The drop visibly exceeds the rim. The inset fades out over 8 frames before the wave in s021. No numbers on screen.

segments.text: Within seconds, the sea rushed {m:rush}in.
segments.visual: At {m:rush}: a local wave surges over the dropped shore from the east (frame right) and fills the low ground; framed at human scale, never as a hero wave; the palms remain, a few low bushes are torn out.

segments.text: {m:two}Two people died.
segments.visual: From {m:two}: hold on our render of the flooded grove at first light: wide, slow drift back, colour desaturated 20%, mean luma 70 or more. No text, no gag, no sting.
segments.music: Single sustained low note; music down 3 dB.

segments.text: By {m:morning}morning, the palm grove was standing in the sea.
segments.visual: [PD] USGS 'Submerged coconut grove at Halapē after 1975 quake' (marked Public Domain, no photographer named; check the credit line), full-bleed in the shared grade, Ken Burns 2%, 3 s max, in on {m:morning}; then back to our render of the same standing grove in the water at first light. The film's first archival still (event evidence, not an idea-history aside). The image ends the beat; no cut to a new topic until the next line.

segments.text: All that, from several {m:yards}yards of sliding.
segments.visual: Pull back to a regional oblique of the Big Island's south side; Kīlauea's south flank gets the hero-orange fill; at {m:yards}: a short yellow arrow points seaward. Never 'just' a few yards.

segments.text: Now picture a whole side of a volcano letting {m:go}go. One {m:did}did.
segments.visual: At {m:go}: whip-pan northwest along the chain (8 frames, motion blur) toward Oʻahu; at {m:did} the whip lands on windward Oʻahu's green cliffs. Chapter card 'OʻAHU'S MISSING SIDE' rides over the moving bright shot (near-opaque plate, 0.26 s in, 1.1 s hold, 0.26 s out); the voice gap covers the card's first 0.9 s.
segments.music: Crossfade to the Ch2 cue: lighter, windy, playful.

segments.text: This is the {m:pali}Pali Lookout, on {m:oahu}Oʻahu.
segments.visual: S3 HERO OBLIQUE settling into a ground shot: Nuʻuanu Pali State Wayside (pin from DLNR/GNIS), the green fluted Koʻolau cliffs, trade-wind clouds streaming over the ridge. Camera behind the lookout wall at about 1,200 ft, looking northeast over the windward side. Map label 'PALI LOOKOUT' at {m:pali}, held 2 s; at {m:oahu} the camera settles behind the wall.

segments.text: Pali means {m:cliff}cliff.
segments.visual: At {m:cliff}: the camera tilts to take in the full height of the cliff face beyond the wall.

segments.text: The wind here is usually so strong, you can {m:lean}lean on it.
segments.visual: The recurring paper tourist (same card as 0:22) stands BEHIND the waist-high stone wall at 35-40% of frame height; the wall stays between him and the drop the whole time. The trade wind blows FROM the northeast, up the cliff, into his face. At {m:lean}: he leans forward into the wind at an absurd 25-30 deg and stays up (paper hinge wobble, shirt flutter); his upper body stays behind the wall line, never out over the edge. Tourist appearance 2 of 4.

segments.text: Hold on to your {m:hat}hat.
segments.visual: GAG (3 s): at {m:hat} his hat lifts off and flies BACKWARD over his head, inland toward Honolulu (physically true for a wind blowing into his face); he turns and runs after it out of frame-left. The camera does NOT follow him: it rises over the wall and dives down the cliff face alone ('(Look Down)' echo, 2 s eased). Nothing and nobody falls off the Pali.
segments.humor: The joke is the wind, not the drop (taste: the 1795 battle). Gust plus a comic paper flap in the gap after the line.

segments.text: If you've stood here, you've stood at the edge of something {m:huge}huge.
segments.visual: The dive levels out and pulls back to a regional oblique of windward Oʻahu from the northeast, 30 km up: the Koʻolau pali reads as one long curved wall. At {m:huge}: a thin white line traces the cliff top. (Comment hook: the pinned comment asks who has stood here.)

segments.text: These cliffs may trace where a volcano tore {m:tore}apart.
segments.visual: At {m:tore}: a soft hero-orange glow runs along the cliff line (the scar). Nothing is drawn offshore yet. (Keep 'may': USGS hedges this.)

segments.text: To find the rest of that volcano, drain the sea {m:ne}northeast of Oʻahu.
segments.visual: At {m:ne}: eased 2.5 s move out to sea: camera about 80 km northeast of Oʻahu, 25 km up, looking southwest back at the island, VE 1.0, low sun from the east so the blocks will throw long shadows, hypsometric seabed tint (never grey mush). The live drain starts (water 0 to -4,500 m over the next 10 s, gauge marker dropping).

segments.text: Past the {m:shelf}shelf. Down the {m:slope}slope.
segments.visual: Same live drain: at {m:shelf} the shallow shelf around Oʻahu surfaces; at {m:slope} the water drops down the island's submarine slope.

segments.text: {m:first}First, the tops of giant blocks. Then {m:more}more blocks. Then a whole {m:field}field of rubble.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK. Same live drain, physically true order (highest points surface first): at {m:first} the tops of the tallest blocks break the falling water surface (the largest summit is at about -2,691 m); at {m:more} more blocks surface one after another (a new one every 1-2 s), spreading northeast; at {m:field} the lower, hummocky debris field emerges around them. Hold the surfacing 3 s longer than the draft (retention backfill): the pause after the line is the held live drain.

segments.text: This is the debris of one of the largest {m:slides}landslides on Earth.
segments.visual: At {m:slides}: the whole debris field (outline traced from USGS I-2809 / Moore et al. 1989, never invented) takes the hero-orange 55% fill and white outline.

segments.text: The volcano that built eastern Oʻahu split right through its {m:summit}summit.
segments.visual: Eased 2 s swing back toward Oʻahu's east side. At {m:summit}: a white line marks where the old summit caldera was cut in two (schematic marker on the real cliffs).

segments.text: Its whole northeast side is lying out {m:outhere}here.
segments.visual: At {m:outhere}: fast eased flight (2 s) from the cliffs out along the real mapped deposit at low altitude; blocks rush past in the foreground (the path is the mapped deposit, never a simulated collapse; no tsunami).

segments.text: Look at this one {m:block}block.
segments.visual: At {m:block}: push in to the largest block (summit about -2,691 m at 22.065N 157.072W; never name it), low sun, long shadow, VE 1.0, water now below its base.

segments.text: It's bigger than {m:manh}Manhattan.
segments.visual: HERO SHOT, S7 TRUE-SIZE DRAG: at {m:manh} a true-scale Manhattan outline (US Census TIGER New York County polygon, public domain; 5-6 px white outline, 40% cyan fill) drops from above and drapes along the block's LONG axis over the WHOLE block (its footprint at about the -4,000 m contour, about 27 x 18 km), VE 1.0. Never place it on the small summit area (above -2,900 m the top is only about 37 km2 and 6 km long; Manhattan is 21.6 km long). Map label 'MANHATTAN' on the outline.

segments.text: With room to {m:spare}spare.
segments.visual: Dry gag (2.5 s): at {m:spare} the outline settles with a tiny 'tok'; a 1.5 s camera rise shows wide bare block on both long sides of the narrow island (the spare room shows mostly in WIDTH: block about 18 km wide, Manhattan about 3.7 km). No turning or sliding around; no 'room on every side' staging.
segments.humor: A true-size drag that fits far too easily. Music dip before the line.

segments.text: The debris runs for more than a hundred {m:miles}miles.
segments.visual: HERO NUMBER #2: pull back to a regional oblique; a 10 px yellow line with a moving head dot draws along the mapped deposit (USGS I-2809) from Oʻahu's coast out to the farthest blocks; at {m:miles} the number block lands: kicker 'MORE THAN', number '100 MILES'.

segments.text: And it's one of dozens of giant slides along this island {m:chain}chain.
segments.visual: Quick pullback over the chain (4 s or less): about 8-10 other giant slide footprints (a sample, traced only from USGS I-2809 / Moore et al. 1989) light up in hero orange one every 0.25 s, finishing on {m:chain}; then they dim to 30%.

segments.text: They're rare. But they {m:happen}happen.
segments.visual: The footprints hold at 30%, then fade after {m:happen}. No interval number, no tsunami.

segments.text: The coast that dropped in the dark? It's part of Kīlauea's south {m:flank}flank.
segments.visual: Eased 2.5 s flight back southeast to the Big Island. At {m:flank}: Kīlauea's south flank outlined in hero orange; map label 'KĪLAUEA'.

segments.text: And it's still {m:creep}creeping toward the sea, a couple of inches a year.
segments.visual: At {m:creep}: small yellow arrows on the flank point seaward and inch forward (no rate, no digits).

segments.text: Not falling. {m:creeping}Creeping.
segments.visual: At {m:creeping}: the arrows keep inching; nothing collapses. Dry button.
segments.humor: Dry laugh in the 2:35-4:00 gap: a 1.0 s music dip (-10 dB) right before 'Creeping'.

segments.text: So how big is the mountain under the Big Island, {m:really}really?
segments.visual: At {m:really}: the camera rises to a high oblique of the whole Big Island, water at 0 m.

segments.text: Let's drain all the way {m:alldown}down.
segments.visual: At {m:alldown}: the drain starts (the water plane begins to fall). Chapter card 'THE ISLAND STANDS UP' over the moving drain shot.
segments.music: Crossfade to the Ch3 cue: big, rising, wide.

segments.text: Drain this far, and the islands stop being {m:isl}islands.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK. S4 GROUND live drain on the Big Island, low camera off the northeast flank (about 35 km northeast of Hilo, 1,000 m above the falling waterline, looking southwest), water -1,000 to -4,000 m over 8 s, gauge marker dropping. At {m:isl}: a quick high pullback (4 s or less) shows that by about -4,000 m every main island from the Big Island to Niʻihau sits on one continuous dry ridge (approximate ETOPO sill check; confirm on the HMRG grid before any label).

segments.text: It's one long mountain {m:range}range.
segments.visual: At {m:range}: a hero-orange line runs along the ridge crest from Hawaiʻi to Niʻihau, then fades.

segments.text: And at this end, the Big Island stands {m:up}up.
segments.visual: Eased 2 s dive back to the Big Island end of the ridge, low camera; at {m:up} the whole massif towers over the frame. Do NOT animate volcanoes merging: they are already one island; the drain only reveals the body. Hold the stand-up 3 s longer than the draft (retention backfill; live drain continues).

segments.text: Several volcanoes grew together into this one {m:mtn}mountain.
segments.visual: At {m:mtn}: the summits of the island's volcanoes each get a brief white pin pulse (no names, no count), then the whole massif one hero-orange outline.

segments.text: Without the ocean, you can finally see its {m:shape}shape.
segments.visual: At {m:shape}: slow lateral move along the base of the massif, low sun raking the real ridges and gullies of the submarine flanks (VE 1.0, HMRG 50 m synthesis blended into ETOPO; real grid relief only, no procedural or noise relief in this shot). The trust line 'Every ridge down here is real.' is CUT (owner's ban on provenance lines); it may come back only with the owner's explicit OK, and never on screen.

segments.text: Today's shoreline is a thin white line, high up its {m:slopes}slopes.
segments.visual: At {m:slopes}: the thin white coast line on the standing massif brightens; the camera holds it in the upper third of frame. At VE 1.0 it sits a little more than halfway up from the moat floor (about 57-59%); never stage it as 'near the top'.

segments.text: Every beach on this island is up {m:upthere}there.
segments.visual: At {m:upthere}: the cap above the white line (the dry island) takes a soft hero-orange tint for 1 s.

segments.text: Below it, the mountain keeps {m:going}going. And {m:going2}going.
segments.visual: '(Look Down)' beat inside the chapter: at {m:going} the camera tilts down the flank from the white line; at {m:going2} it keeps tilting, down and down to the base.

segments.text: Along its east side, the sea floor dips into a deep {m:trench}trench.
segments.visual: Water continues to about -5,500 m. The last water is the real strip in the Hawaiian Deep, from north of Molokaʻi and Maui to about 100 km east of Hilo (flood-fill at the shot's level on the real grid; west and south-west of the island are dry; NO sculpted ring). At {m:trench}: the leftover band glows bright cyan.

segments.text: Remember that {m:rem}trench. It's a {m:clue}clue.
segments.visual: At {m:rem}: slow push toward the cyan strip; at {m:clue} one soft pulse. No label. LOOP PLANTED: paid at s161 and s167 ('That trench at its feet is the edge of that dent').

segments.text: Now bring in {m:ev}Everest, at the same scale.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK. S4 comparison shot, VE 1.0, camera about 120 km to the north, 70 mm, low. At {m:ev} the SRTM Everest mesh rises (3 s, rumble) beside the massif STANDING ON THE SEA-LEVEL LINE (a thin white horizontal line across both; Everest on a plain pedestal so it stands its full 8,849 m; never the 5,000 m base cut). Map label 'EVEREST'.

segments.text: Above sea level, Everest wins {m:easily}easily.
segments.visual: At {m:easily}: above the white sea-level line, Everest's peak (8,849 m) towers over Mauna Kea's cap (4,205 m). True as staged: both stand on the same sea-level line here.

segments.text: But measured from the sea {m:seafloor}floor, Mauna Kea is more than thirty-three thousand feet {m:tall33}tall.
segments.visual: HERO NUMBER #3. At {m:seafloor}: Everest sinks 6,000 m (eased 1.2 s) so its base sits on the shared USGS base line at -6,000 m beside Mauna Kea's foot (its peak now at about +2,849 m); the EVEREST label fades. The yellow height bar starts at that same base line and climbs Mauna Kea while the counter rolls; it lands '33,000+ FT' exactly on {m:tall33} (a label, never driven by the rendered moat floor). Kicker 'FROM THE SEA FLOOR' (4 words: logged exception to the look book's 2-word kicker cap, because the qualifier is mandatory, ledger C3-01 and PLAYBOOK_craft 9). Map label 'MAUNA KEA' on the summit. Visible words 8 of 10.

segments.text: That's taller than {m:ev2}Everest.
segments.visual: At {m:ev2}: the bar's top passes Everest's summit on the same base line; a thin white tick marks Everest's top; Mauna Kea's summit stands clearly higher.

segments.text: You may have heard that {m:heard}one.
segments.visual: At {m:heard}: JUICE CHECK stamp 'TRUE' (S13, 1.2 s) over the still-moving comparison shot.

segments.text: On Everest, getting to the top looks like {m:this}this.
segments.visual: GAG part 1 (3 s), S11 on Everest's summit (SRTM terrain, real snow): at {m:this} a paper cut-out climber (public-domain photo, for example an NPS mountaineering photo; down suit, oxygen mask; not a named person) at 35-40% of frame height, frost on the card edge, plants a small flag while the card shudders in the wind.

segments.text: There's a road almost to the top of this {m:road}one.
segments.visual: GAG part 2: at {m:road} whip-pan (8 frames) to Mauna Kea's summit access road on the upper slope, well below the summit area: a paper 4WD (public-domain photo) rolls up the road with a little dust. Whip back: the climber's flag droops on its paper hinge. No car or figure on Puʻuwēkiu, no telescope joke; the domes are never the punchline.
segments.humor: The joke lands on the climber's ordeal. Music dip before the line; comic 'deflate' in the gap after it.

segments.text: But Mauna Kea isn't the giant {m:giant}here.
segments.visual: At {m:giant}: eased 2 s orbit to the southwest of the massif; Mauna Kea dims.

segments.text: Its neighbor, {m:loa}Mauna Loa, is a little lower, and far {m:bigger}bigger.
segments.visual: At {m:loa}: Mauna Loa's whole edifice, above and below the old waterline, takes the hero-orange fill and white outline; map label 'MAUNA LOA'. At {m:bigger}: the fill swells across its full broad mass beside the dimmed Mauna Kea.

segments.text: It's the largest {m:active}active volcano on Earth.
segments.visual: At {m:active}: headline 'LARGEST ACTIVE VOLCANO' (the qualifier 'ACTIVE' always stays) in the free third.

segments.text: It covers about half of this {m:half}island.
segments.visual: 3 s cut to TODAY's island at sea level, high oblique: Mauna Loa's above-sea outline (USGS geologic map) fills in hero orange and the other volcanoes' areas in dim white; at {m:half} the orange reads as about half of the island (it is about 50/50: never stage it as outweighing the rest).

segments.text: And even now, we haven't seen all of {m:allofit}it.
segments.visual: Back to the drained massif; at {m:allofit} the camera lowers toward Mauna Loa's base, where the slope disappears into the trench shadow; slow push. (Loop: re-planted at s085, paid at the payoff.)

segments.text: But this giant can't {m:stay}stay. It's already {m:moving}moving.
segments.visual: TWIST. At {m:stay}: S4 cut-away under the Big Island: a glowing hot spot below (picture only, no labels; the ONLY time this glow cut-away is shown). At {m:moving}: the plate carrying the island begins to slide northwest off the glow.

segments.text: Picture a {m:candle}candle under a sheet of paper.
segments.visual: Physical metaphor in motion (the whole mechanism about 20 s, no jargon on screen): at {m:candle}, in the same cut-away, the plate becomes a sheet of paper and the glow becomes a candle flame beneath it, in the same place.

segments.text: Slide the paper, and the flame scorches a line of {m:spots}spots.
segments.visual: The paper slides; a line of scorch marks forms; at {m:spots} the marks cross-dissolve (0.5 s) into the real island chain at chain oblique.

segments.text: The paper is the Pacific {m:plate}plate. The flame is a hot spot, deep {m:deepbelow}below.
segments.visual: Back on the real Earth: at {m:plate} the Pacific plate takes a 35% hero-orange tint and a big yellow arrow (15 px body, 50-63 px head) points northwest along the chain; at {m:deepbelow}: a small warm marker pulses at the hot spot's position under the Big Island (map marker, not a second cut-away; no 'plume from the core').

segments.text: So the island rides away from the heat that {m:built}built it.
segments.visual: At {m:built}: the Big Island's outline edges northwest, off the warm marker.

segments.text: And as it goes, it {m:sinks}sinks.
segments.visual: At {m:sinks}: hard cut to the drained west (Kohala) flank at low raking light.

segments.text: See those {m:steps}steps on the island's side? They're old coral {m:reefs}reefs.
segments.visual: S4 GROUND close on the drowned-reef terraces off west Hawaiʻi (the documented series off Kohala; draw or highlight steps only where the bathymetry really shows terraces). At {m:steps}: the terrace edges catch the light; at {m:reefs}: a thin cream highlight runs along each step.

segments.text: They grew at the shoreline, and the island sank out from under {m:them}them.
segments.visual: Short schematic loop on one step (3 s): a reef grows at the waterline, then the step and the reef ride down as the water line stays; at {m:them} the next reef starts at the new shoreline above.

segments.text: The deepest ones are now thousands of feet {m:deepreef}down.
segments.visual: At {m:deepreef}: the camera tilts down the flank along the lowest terraces into the blue (no depth text; mean luma 70 or more).

segments.text: Every island to the northwest was born right {m:bornhere}here.
segments.visual: At {m:bornhere}: regional pullback (4 s or less) along the chain to the northwest; each main island takes a brief hero-orange rim in turn (Maui, Oʻahu, Kauaʻi).

segments.text: Each one is older than the {m:last}last.
segments.visual: At {m:last}: the rims fade in order of age, youngest to oldest.

segments.text: That makes the Big Island the baby of the {m:baby}islands. A very big {m:bigbaby}baby.
segments.visual: At {m:baby}: the Big Island alone takes a hero-orange rim at the young end of the chain. At {m:bigbaby}: crash zoom OUT (8 frames, motion blur) to a frame where the Big Island visibly outweighs all the older islands put together (true: about 10,430 km2 against about 6,400 km2 for the rest).
segments.humor: Dry button in the mid-film laugh gap. 1.0 s music dip before 'A very big baby'; tiny comic 'boing' on the crash zoom.

segments.text: And each one shows what this island will {m:become}become.
segments.visual: At {m:become}: the camera settles back on the Big Island. Chapter card 'WATCH IT GROW OLD' over the moving shot.
segments.music: Crossfade to the Ch4 cue: travelling, steady pulse.

segments.text: So let's ride the plate, and watch the Big Island grow {m:old}old.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK, THE TIME MACHINE (the film's second engine). For this chapter the top-left gauge becomes an AGE gauge (same corner and plate; a yellow marker on a slim bar, starting at 'NOW'). At {m:old}: the camera lifts off the Big Island at regional oblique.

segments.text: Then we'll come back for the part we haven't {m:notseen}seen.
segments.visual: At {m:notseen}: a 1 s glance down the drained south flank into the dark of the trench (no text), then the camera swings to the south coast. LOOP RE-PLANTED (the payoff's forward promise across the 4:47 tour).

segments.text: First stop: its own {m:coast}coast. The sea is already wearing it down.
segments.visual: Eased flight down; at {m:coast} the camera arrives at the Big Island's south coast near the end of Chain of Craters Road, water at 0 m, surf breaking white against black lava sea cliffs (real 10 m DEM, true colour).

segments.text: This September, a sea arch on this coast {m:arch}collapsed into the ocean.
segments.visual: Before/after from two DATED National Park Service photos of the Hōlei Sea Arch (standing, and the gap after the 23-27 Sept 2026 collapse; NPS photos are usually public domain but some are by volunteers, so check each credit line), shown as one 3.5 s wipe in the shared grade with a slow Ken Burns; the wipe lands on {m:arch}. Map label 'HŌLEI SEA ARCH' (the name is shown, not narrated, to remove a pronunciation risk). No cause shown or implied; nothing ties it to sinking. Counts as this stretch's archival moment.

segments.text: Waves had carved it out of lava over {m:cent}centuries.
segments.visual: At {m:cent}: back on our terrain, waves wash through the coast where the arch stood; slow pull back up and away.

segments.text: Give the Big Island time, and it looks like {m:maui2}Maui.
segments.visual: Eased flight northwest lands on Maui (Haleakalā fills the frame; real island at its real position, no morphing). At {m:maui2}: map label 'MAUI'; the age marker slides right.

segments.text: Older still: {m:oahu2}Oʻahu, home of {m:hnl}Honolulu. Here, a whole side of a volcano slid into the sea.
segments.visual: Flight to Oʻahu's windward side, the Koʻolau cliffs and the debris field offshore. At {m:oahu2}: map label 'OʻAHU'; at {m:hnl} a small pin pulses on Honolulu (no second label). Callback GAG (2 s): back at the Pali Lookout, the paper tourist now holds his hat on with both hands, still behind the wall. Tourist appearance 3 of 4.

segments.text: Older still: {m:kauai}Kauaʻi. Its big eruptions ended long ago, and rain has carved it into {m:canyons}canyons.
segments.visual: Flight to Kauaʻi. At {m:kauai}: map label 'KAUAʻI'; at {m:canyons}: the camera drops into the red walls of Waimea Canyon while a rain squall sweeps over the rim and water threads down the gullies.

segments.text: After that, the islands get smaller and {m:lower}lower.
segments.visual: At {m:lower}: fast eased flight northwest past Niʻihau and out over open ocean; the age marker keeps sliding right.

segments.text: This is {m:nihoa}Nihoa.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK. Nihoa fills the frame: a small steep island with tall sea cliffs. At {m:nihoa}: map label 'NIHOA'.

segments.text: {m:seven}Seven million years in, it's a sliver of {m:rock}rock.
segments.visual: HERO NUMBER #4: at {m:seven} the AGE gauge marker lands and the number block lands: kicker 'ABOUT', number '7 MILLION YEARS' (Anton, yellow); at {m:rock} the camera pulls wide to show how little is left; the block fades before the next line.

segments.text: Even so, it's the biggest volcanic island left out {m:outhere2}here.
segments.visual: At {m:outhere2}: a quick eased pull-out over the open northwest chain: nothing else above water comes close (a dry, true irony; no label, no number).
segments.humor: Dry irony: a sliver, and still the biggest.

segments.text: And people {m:lived}lived here.
segments.visual: At {m:lived}: slow push into Nihoa's terraced valleys; music softens.

segments.text: Centuries ago, they built homes, farm terraces and shrines on this {m:shrine}rock.
segments.visual: On our terrain: house and terrace sites appear as soft white outlines ONLY where drawn from a published site map (otherwise marked approximate or left out), landing on {m:shrine}. No archival still here (it would fall under 60 s after the Hōlei photos). No gags (there are burials).

segments.text: And they buried their dead {m:dead}here.
segments.visual: At {m:dead}: slow drift over the terraces in late light; no markers, no SFX; music softens further.

segments.text: Today, nobody lives {m:nobody}here.
segments.visual: At {m:nobody}: wind over empty rock; seabird specks; pull away.

segments.text: Farther on: French Frigate {m:ffs}Shoals. In Hawaiian, {m:lalo}Lalo.
segments.visual: Eased flight northwest to the lagoon at Lalo. At {m:ffs}: one map label 'LALO' fades in and holds 3 s, through {m:lalo} (both names are spoken; the label carries the Hawaiian one).

segments.text: Only one rock of its volcano still stands above the sea. Its last {m:tooth}tooth.
segments.visual: Close oblique on the lone basalt pinnacle standing out of the lagoon; at {m:tooth}: hero-orange outline on the pinnacle; map label 'LA PÉROUSE PINNACLE' (label only, not narrated). No height spoken or shown.

segments.text: This strip of sand was East {m:east}Island.
segments.visual: BEFORE state, from dated imagery (July 2018): East Island's sandy outline at low oblique; map label 'EAST ISLAND' at {m:east}. The picture runs before-to-after ONCE in this beat.

segments.text: Endangered Hawaiian monk seals came here to rest and raise {m:pups}pups.
segments.visual: Still the before state: a paper Hawaiian monk seal (public-domain NOAA photo; grey-brown, no ear flaps) resting on the sand at 35-40% of frame height; at {m:pups} a pup shape shuffles in beside it, on the real terrain with contact shadows and the same sun.

segments.text: Only about sixteen hundred are {m:left}left.
segments.visual: At {m:left}: the seal lifts its head toward camera; slow push. No number on screen.

segments.text: Then, not long ago, a hurricane passed right over these {m:shoals}shoals.
segments.visual: At {m:shoals}: a storm spiral (soft cloud texture, true colour, no category label) comes in from the SOUTH-SOUTHWEST moving north-northeast; its eye passes just WEST of the atoll and its eastern eyewall sweeps across the lagoon (2 s). Physically true to the NHC track.

segments.text: It washed almost all of East Island {m:away}away.
segments.visual: At {m:away}: wipe to the AFTER state from dated imagery (October 2018): East Island is a sliver. Then GAG (3 s) in the pause: the seal swims up to where its beach was, finds water, bobs, looks left, looks right (paper turn), blinks. Nothing implies a seal was hurt. No 'overnight', no storm category.
segments.humor: The seal comes home and the beach is missing. Music dip; tiny comic 'bloop' in the gap.

segments.text: Since then, the sand has been coming {m:sandback}back.
segments.visual: At {m:sandback}: time-lapse from the monthly shorelines: the sand outline regrows to about half its old size (no percent on screen); keep it bare (no vegetation).

segments.text: And so have the {m:seals}seals.
segments.visual: At {m:seals}: the seal flops onto the regrown sandbar and settles; two more seals haul out beside it (real terrain, contact shadows, same sun).
segments.humor: Twist on the gag: the seals came back.

segments.text: Farther on, one last pair of rocks pokes {m:pokes}out.
segments.visual: Flight northwest: at {m:pokes} the Gardner Pinnacles appear, two small basalt rocks in open sea; map label 'PŪHĀHONU (GARDNER PINNACLES)' (label only).

segments.text: After that, no volcanic rock reaches the surface at {m:atall}all.
segments.visual: At {m:atall}: the flight continues northwest over open water; the AGE marker slides on; pale reef rings appear ahead.

segments.text: Only {m:onlyreef}reef.
segments.visual: At {m:onlyreef}: arrival over a ring of reef. Chapter card 'FOUGHT OVER A VOLCANO' over the moving shot.
segments.music: Crossfade to the Ch5 cue: bright, open, a little mischievous.

segments.text: This ring of reef is {m:midway}Midway.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK. S3 HERO OBLIQUE: Midway Atoll (28.21N 177.37W), true colour, the reef ring and Sand Island at regional oblique. At {m:midway}: map label 'MIDWAY'. The top-left gauge is the SEA LEVEL gauge again.

segments.text: It's farther from Honolulu than {m:ny}New York is from {m:miami}Miami.
segments.visual: S7 TRUE-SIZE DRAG on a STORY globe filling the frame height (8 s or less, proof-overlay exception): a 10 px white line draws from Honolulu to Midway; at {m:ny} the true-length great-circle line from New York to Miami (1,092 mi) lifts off the US East Coast with a drag whoosh; at {m:miami} it lands beside the Honolulu-Midway line (1,312 mi) and visibly comes up short (no distance labels, no digits). Then back down to the atoll.

segments.text: It has the biggest albatross colony on {m:earth}Earth.
segments.visual: At {m:earth}: dive to Sand Island at ground level: a field of nesting albatrosses as small shapes; one paper Laysan albatross (public-domain USFWS photo) in the foreground at 35-40% of frame height; map label 'LAYSAN ALBATROSS' for 2 s.

segments.text: In the air, they're {m:grace}graceful.
segments.visual: At {m:grace}: the paper albatross glides across the frame, wings out, smooth.

segments.text: Landing is another {m:story}story.
segments.visual: GAG (3 s): at {m:story} the albatross comes in to land in a light wind, wings out, and tumbles into a forward roll on the sand (believable, on the real terrain); dust puff; it ends upright and ruffled.
segments.humor: The clumsy landing. Music dip before the line; comic thump in the gap.

segments.text: Here, they're known as gooney {m:gooney}birds.
segments.visual: At {m:gooney}: the bird shakes its head; slow pull back up to the atoll, where the water starts to fall around the reef (the held live drain of s118 starts in this pause).

segments.text: Under this reef lies a volcano about twenty-eight million years {m:old28}old.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK, HERO NUMBER #5. Drain plus cut-away (S4 'cake cut'): the water falls around the atoll, then the atoll is sliced open: a dark basalt volcano under a thick cream reef cap. At {m:old28}: number block 'ABOUT 28 MILLION YEARS' with a thin pointer to the basalt (the age belongs to the volcano, not the reef). Hold the cut-away drain 3 s longer than the draft (retention backfill).

segments.text: As it sank, the reef on top kept growing {m:upward}upward.
segments.visual: At {m:upward}: the cut-away animates: the volcano sinks in uneven steps (pauses between them, never smooth) and the reef cap grows upward to stay at the surface.

segments.text: Charles {m:darwin}Darwin came up with this idea: reefs like this sit on sinking islands.
segments.visual: Told on OUR cut-away (not the 1842 woodcut, to keep archival stills 60 s apart): the same atoll cut-away replays its sink-and-grow loop in 3 s while a name plate 'CHARLES DARWIN' slides in at {m:darwin}. No portrait, no book page.

segments.text: Long after he died, drills here went down through hundreds of feet of reef {m:reefrock}rock.
segments.visual: Cut-away: two drill strings (Sand Island, and the north rim of the lagoon) descend through the cream reef rock, reaching the bottom of it on {m:reefrock}; the basalt top sits about 515 ft under Sand Island and deepens to about 1,250 ft under the north rim (optional thin clay band on the basalt). No depth numbers on screen.

segments.text: And hit the {m:hitvolc}volcano.
segments.visual: At {m:hitvolc}: the bits strike basalt; a spark flash on the basalt top (one flash).

segments.text: In June {m:y1942}nineteen forty-two, a battle was fought over this sunken {m:volc42}volcano.
segments.visual: TWIST, RE-HOOK. Hard cut back to the atoll from above, water restored, early-morning light. At {m:y1942}: kicker 'JUNE 1942'. At {m:volc42}: the reef ring takes a thin hero-orange rim.
segments.music: Ch5 cue switches section to a taut pulse (story turn).

segments.text: It turned the war in the {m:pac}Pacific.
segments.visual: At {m:pac}: pull out to a regional S2 STORY map of the central Pacific centred on Midway.

segments.text: And part of the story is a fake complaint about {m:water0}water.
segments.visual: At {m:water0}: a paper water-drop icon pops on Midway's pin and wobbles (story humour; no one has died yet).

segments.text: Weeks before, American codebreakers kept seeing one target in intercepted {m:msgs}messages: {m:af}AF.
segments.visual: At {m:msgs}: coded radio traffic drawn as scrambled glyph streams crossing the map; at {m:af}: the letters 'AF' light up yellow inside the stream.

segments.text: They were fairly sure AF was Midway. Washington {m:wasnt}wasn't.
segments.visual: At {m:wasnt}: a small paper telegram flutters from the Hawaiʻi side of the map toward the edge of frame (toward Washington), then flutters back with a paper question-mark tag (no readable text).

segments.text: So they had Midway radio a message in plain {m:plain}language.
segments.visual: At {m:plain}: a clean, readable radio ring pulses out from Midway into the air (no cable drawn; the cable detail is dropped).

segments.text: The {m:bait}bait: its fresh-water plant had broken {m:broke}down.
segments.visual: At {m:bait}: a paper water-drop dangles from a paper fishing line off Midway's pin; at {m:broke}: a paper water tank on Sand Island gives a sad little wobble and a drip. Reported speech: no quote marks and no message text on screen or in captions (accounts word it differently).
segments.humor: Deadpan fake complaint, told as bait.

segments.text: Japan {m:bit}bit. A coded Japanese report passed it {m:along}along.
segments.visual: At {m:bit}: the paper fishing line twitches with a tiny tug; then a scrambled glyph stream travels back across the map; at {m:along} it starts to decode.
segments.humor: 'Japan bit': the trick lands in one word.

segments.text: AF is short of {m:shortwater}water.
segments.visual: At {m:shortwater}: the glyph stream settles (no text block; this line is never captioned in quote marks).
segments.humor: The punchline is the enemy repeating the fake plea. Music dip -10 dB under the line.

segments.text: That {m:conf}confirmed it. AF was {m:mid2}Midway.
segments.visual: At {m:conf}: the question-mark tag falls off the telegram; at {m:mid2}: 'AF = MIDWAY' lands beside Midway's pin with a soft thunk (not the Juice Check stamp). In the 1.2 s pause the comedy ends: the paper props fade and the map darkens slightly toward the open ocean.
segments.music: Music cue changes in the pause: the playful pulse ends; a low, respectful pad begins. No gags from here through the war graves.

segments.text: Japan lost every carrier in its strike {m:force}force.
segments.visual: At {m:force}: the story map pulls out to open ocean north and west of Midway; four simple home-built Japanese carrier silhouettes fade down to dark grey one after another (no flames, no explosions).

segments.text: America lost the carrier {m:york}Yorktown.
segments.visual: At {m:york}: [PD] NHHC photo of USS Yorktown (check the catalog credit line; some NHHC images are donated), full-bleed, Ken Burns 2%, 3 s max.

segments.text: Already crippled, it was sunk by a Japanese {m:sub}submarine.
segments.visual: At {m:sub}: back on the map, the Yorktown silhouette fades down to dark grey (no explosion, no torpedo animation).

segments.text: {m:york2}Yorktown, {m:kaga}Kaga and {m:akagi}Akagi have since been found.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK. Back on the map: one respectful wreck marker (home-built hull silhouette, 64 px or more) per name, each at its RECORDED 1942 sinking position (Yorktown 30°35'59"N 176°34'04"W; Akagi 30°30'N 178°40'W; Kaga 30°23'N 179°17'W; approximate at chain scale). Names: ONE text block whose three words reveal whole on their spoken words (YORKTOWN at {m:york2}, KAGA at {m:kaga}, AKAGI at {m:akagi}) and hold together at least 2.5 s; each marker pulses on its word. Never three separate map labels.

segments.text: Drain the sea, and you'd find them nowhere near the {m:atoll}atoll.
segments.visual: Drain the ocean around Midway on the GEBCO chain terrain; at {m:atoll} a thick yellow line (10 px core, dark under-stroke) draws from the atoll to each wreck marker; its length shows the distance (no distance labels, no coordinates).

segments.text: They lie far out, more than three miles {m:threemi}down, on the deep ocean floor.
segments.visual: HERO NUMBER #6, quiet: inset zoom (the wrecks are tiny at chain scale): low camera on the deep ocean floor (gentle abyssal hills, not flat), one hull silhouette resting in a LIT POOL of soft blue light (mean luma 70 or more; no run over 4 s below luma 40, a dark stretch reads as buffering on a phone). At {m:threemi}: the SEA LEVEL gauge goes to hero mode with kicker 'MORE THAN' and number '3 MILES DOWN', a soft tick only (no impact hit: war graves).

segments.text: These are war graves, for American and Japanese sailors {m:alike}alike.
segments.visual: At {m:alike}: hold, slow drift around the lit pool; the number block has faded. No gags, no 'treasure', no gore.
segments.music: Soft pad, then lift into the Kure section after the pause.

segments.text: Past Midway lies {m:kure}Kure, the last atoll in the chain.
segments.visual: Eased flight northwest to Kure Atoll (28.39N 178.29W), water restored, reef ring. At {m:kure}: map label 'KURE (HŌLANIKŪ)' (label only, the Hawaiian name is not narrated).

segments.text: Darwin never saw it. But on his reef map, he colored it {m:blue}blue.
segments.visual: Told on OUR map (no archival crop: a world-map crop of the 1842 map is unreadable at 390 px and would break the 60 s still spacing): Kure fills at least a third of the frame at regional oblique; at {m:blue} its reef ring takes a soft cyan-blue tint (35-40%). No old-map pastiche, no fake document.

segments.text: Blue meant a reef on sinking {m:sinkground}ground.
segments.visual: At {m:sinkground}: one text block, 'BLUE = SINKING' (BLUE in cyan, the coloured word is the legend; 3 words), 2 s, while the ring holds its tint; a slow push toward the reef edge.

segments.text: Here the water is so cool, the reef can barely keep up with the {m:sinking}sinking.
segments.visual: Cut-away under Kure: the reef cap just keeping pace at the surface while the volcano sinks; at {m:sinking} the reef's top flickers at the waterline.

segments.text: Scientists call this line the Darwin {m:point}Point.
segments.visual: At {m:point}: a thin hero-orange line across the chain at about 29N lights up; map label 'DARWIN POINT'. (Pays the Darwin plant.)

segments.text: Past it, every island has {m:drowned2}drowned.
segments.visual: At {m:drowned2}: the water drains northwest of Kure (GEBCO): drowned flat-topped seamounts appear beyond the line.

segments.text: That's the road the Big Island is {m:roadon}on.
segments.visual: At {m:roadon}: a faint hero-orange ghost of the Big Island's outline appears for 1.5 s beside one drowned seamount past the line (its fate, not a place), then fades.

segments.text: The drowned volcanoes {m:bend}bend north and march on, all the way to {m:kam}Kamchatka.
segments.visual: S2 STORY globe filling the frame height (4 s or less): the Hawaiian-Emperor chain lit in hero orange; at {m:bend} the bend lights up; at {m:kam} the line reaches Kamchatka; map label 'KAMCHATKA' on the peninsula. No bend age, no cause for the bend.

segments.text: There, the sea floor dives back into the Earth, and takes them with {m:takes}it.
segments.visual: Close globe cut-away at the far end: at {m:takes} the plate slides down into the trench, carrying the last seamount down with it (no text, or at most 'TRENCH').

segments.text: But every volcano in this chain had to start {m:somewhere}somewhere.
segments.visual: At {m:somewhere}: whip back down the chain toward the Big Island (3 s or less). Chapter card 'WE HAVEN'T HIT BOTTOM' over the moving shot (the card pays the cold-open line 'we won't hit bottom').
segments.music: Crossfade to the Ch6 cue: deep, building toward the payoff.

segments.text: Back to the start of the line: the Big Island's south {m:coast6}coast.
segments.visual: RE-HOOK. At {m:coast6}: fast eased flight southeast (2.5 s) down to the Big Island's south flank; water drained to about -1,500 m so the young volcano's top stands exposed; SEA LEVEL gauge back top-left.

segments.text: Off this coast, under the sea, a young volcano is {m:growing}growing.
segments.visual: At {m:growing}: the gauge marker drops to the young volcano's summit level (no digits: its depth is neither spoken nor shown as a number, keeping the 90 s before the payoff clear). The volcano is rendered from the real bathymetry as an ELONGATED RIDGE with a summit platform and pit craters (never a neat cone), about 30 km south of Kīlauea's coast (18°55'12"N 155°16'12"W).

segments.text: Its name is {m:kama}Kamaʻehuakanaloa.
segments.visual: Map label 'KAMAʻEHUAKANALOA' fades in 4 frames before {m:kama} and stays at least 2.5 s. Own take, speed 0.9, about 0.5 s of silence before it, no other new proper noun within 10 s either side.

segments.text: It means reddish child of {m:kanaloa}Kanaloa.
segments.visual: At {m:kanaloa}: slow orbit along the ridge in warm low light; the KAMAʻEHUAKANALOA label is still up (no second label). Respectful beat: no gag, no SFX on the name.

segments.text: This summer, it set off an earthquake people felt across the island's {m:south}south.
